messages:
Priya Nair: FYI — Acme sent an escalation: rerank endpoint returning different scores for identical inputs after last model deploy. Customer says their QA tests (stable for months) now show ~10-15% of queries with flipped top-1 between yesterday and today. They attached sample batch.

Priya Nair: Customer details: org_id=acme_corp, app=search, endpoint=/v1/rerank, observed at ~2026-03-12T14:33Z. They reported no change on their side.

Priya Nair: Sample (sanitized) request they used:
```json
{
  "model": "redwood-rerank-v2.4.0",
  "queries": ["how to reset password"],
  "candidates": ["Reset via profile > security","Contact support to reset","Use forgot-password link"],
  "options": {"return_scores": true}
}
```

Priya Nair: Responses they got yesterday (v2.3.1):
```json
{"ranks": ["Use forgot-password link","Reset via profile > security","Contact support to reset"], "scores": [0.82, 0.56, 0.22]}
```

Priya Nair: Today (after deploy to v2.4.0):
```json
{"ranks": ["Reset via profile > security","Use forgot-password link","Contact support to reset"], "scores": [0.77, 0.74, 0.21]}
```

Priya Nair: Customer is upset because this changed downstream UX (wrong top hit) and they have a scheduled release. Asking for root cause + mitigation asap.

Alex Chen: Can we reproduce internally? Priya, can you paste the exact curl they used or ask them to run with `--dump-header`? Also which deployment region and whether they were using Dedicated or Hosted?

Priya Nair: They confirmed Hosted (us-east-1), traffic small. They ran a simple curl: 
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \ 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' \ 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ 
  -d @payload.json
```
where payload.json is the JSON above. No special headers.

Samir Patel: Reproduced locally against a snapshot of their payload. I ran two calls: one against v2.3.1 (pinned snapshot) and v2.4.0 (prod). I see the flip for ~12/100 samples, mostly short queries. I pasted raw outputs to the incident thread in the support ticket.

Samir Patel: Quick notes from the logs: request_id=req_0a9f3, latency roughly equal, no 4xx/5xx. Scores differ by small margins for top items (0.82->0.77, 0.74). Looks like ranking calibration shifted.

Amelia Reyes: @Nate any recent changes in the rerank model training or postprocessing between v2.3.1 -> v2.4.0? Also any tokenizer or normalization changes?

Nate Olson: Short summary: v2.4.0 included a calibration pass to better spread scores for long-tail queries and a tokenizer normalization tweak (lowercasing + extra punctuation normalization) to reduce duplicates. There was also a small change in the reranker loss mixing weight (increase in pairwise term). None were expected to flip top-1 for well-formed short queries, but small score adjustments can reorder near-ties.

Nate Olson: Hypothesis: the tokenizer normalization made candidate strings more similar in embedding space for some cases, tightening scores. Combined with the heavier pairwise weight, the model prefers slightly different features. Working on a delta test now.

SupportBot: New ticket created: TKT-2026-3345 for Acme rerank regression. Assigned to @Samir Patel, priority P1.

Priya Nair: Customer asking for mitigation: possibilities I outlined — pin to v2.3.1 for them only (can we route by org_id?), rollback global deploy, or provide a quick prompt-engineering workaround (add tie-breaker signals). Which is least risky?

Alex Chen: We can do per-org routing in Hosted today — create a policy to force acme_corp -> model: redwood-rerank-v2.3.1. That buys time. Operationally it's a config change: 
```json
{"route_policies": [{"org_id": "acme_corp", "model": "redwood-rerank-v2.3.1"} ]}
```
I'll open a routing PR and patch config on us-east-1.

Samir Patel: I'd prefer per-org pin first. Rollback is heavy and affects other customers. Also I'll add a temporary precision tie-breaker in the service layer for the rerank endpoint: if top-two scores within 0.05 and one candidate contains exact query tokens, boost that candidate by small epsilon. That should surface the more user-expected result. Will test.

Nate Olson: I'll run an A/B on a 1% sample with both models + tie-breaker rule to quantify delta in offline metrics (MRR, top1 change rate). If we see unacceptable regressions, we'll schedule a rollback.

Amelia Reyes: Can we get a quick diff of calibration-only vs tokenizer-only effects? If tokenizer is the culprit we can revert it quickly. Nate, how fast can you produce a model build with tokenizer=old?

Nate Olson: Tokenizer revert build is fairly quick — ~2 hours to bake and smoke test in staging. Calibration param revert requires retraining mix weights — that's a bit longer (1-2 days) to validate.

Priya Nair: Customer says they need a mitigation within 4 hours. Alex, can you get the per-org routing live in <2h? Samir, can you push a service-layer tie-breaker as a hotfix in the same window?

Alex Chen: Yep, I'll push the routing change and verify traffic goes to v2.3.1. Will update with rollout ts.

Samir Patel: I'll prototype tie-breaker now. Quick patch and will run unit + integration test. If it's safe, I'll feature-flag it on us-east for acme_corp only.

Nate Olson: Started the A/B job. Will share metric snapshot in ~90 minutes.

Priya Nair: Keeping Acme updated: told them we have a mitigation plan (per-org pin + optional tie-breaker) and expect an update in ~2 hours. They're relieved but want postmortem details.

Alex Chen: Routing PR: PR#5742 created, config applied to staging. Will promote to prod after one smoke call.

Samir Patel: Hotfix tie-breaker patch pushed to staging. Test runs: on the customer's sample set, tie-breaker restored top-1 to previous ordering for 9/12 of the flipped cases. No failing unit tests.

SupportBot: Deployment job started: deploy/job/12981 for us-east-1.

Samir Patel: Deployed tie-breaker to us-east with org filter acme_corp. Ran a set of 200 sampled customer queries — top1 flip rate down from 12% -> 1.5%. Sharing raw logs to ticket.

Priya Nair: Customer confirms improvement on their end. They will run their regression suite and report back.

Nate Olson: A/B results: MRR delta for general population is -0.3% (acceptable), for short queries the delta is -1.1% unless tie-breaker applied. Tokenizer-only revert test shows the majority of flips are explained by normalization changes — reverting tokenizer in staging recreates pre-deploy scores.

Amelia Reyes: Action items:
- Alex: keep org pin for acme_corp until we ship a proper fix (or uplifted model).
- Nate: produce tokenizer-reverted build and run full validation (ETA 2h).
- Samir: keep tie-breaker feature-flagged for acme_corp as temporary.
- Priya: coordinate customer comms + postmortem.

Priya Nair: I'll draft the incident summary for Acme and prepare a postmortem that covers root cause (tokenizer normalization change interacting with calibration pass), mitigation timeline, and follow-ups (improve canary tests for rerank top1 stability on seeded regressions).

Priya Nair: Thanks everyone. I'll update thread when Acme completes their regression suite or if we decide to roll back globally. :thumbsup:

SupportBot: Ticket TKT-2026-3345 updated: status=mitigated, owner=Samir Patel, sla=72h.
